title: Local relative fibre dimension of an algebraic space over a scheme
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $T$, with structural morphism $f:X\to T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a chart $a:h_U\to X$, write $g_U:U\to T$ for its composite with the structural morphism. Use the field-valued point classes $|X|$ and scheme point maps $|a|$ of [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes]. For $x\in |X|$, define its local relative fibre dimension by
$$\delta_f(x)=\sup_{(U,a,u)}\dim_{\widetilde u}(U_{g_U(u)}).$$
Here $U$ is an affine scheme over $T$, $a:h_U\to X$ is representable etale in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space], $u\in U$ satisfies $|a|(u)=x$, $U_{g_U(u)}$ is the scheme fibre of $U\to T$ over the image of $u$, and $\widetilde u$ is its unique point above $u$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The dimension of this scheme fibre at that point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. The supremum takes values in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$, with empty supremum $-\infty$. No local finite type or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed on this definition.
